facts.audience: Busy parents who book check-ups for their kids
facts.problem: Appointments get missed and the chair sits empty
facts.cause: The only reminder is an email sent the evening before, which is easy to miss. Nobody's fault.
facts.solution: A text reminder two days ahead that patients can reply to, to confirm or reschedule
facts.outcome: When someone can't make it, they can tell the practice early, so the slot can be offered to another patient

steps.label: Slot kept or offered to another patient

easy to miss
chapters.narration: Our one evening email was easy to miss.

chapters.kicker: A TEXT YOU CAN REPLY TO
headline: Text two days ahead
reply to reschedule
chapters.narration: Now we text two days ahead. Reply, and we can offer your slot to another patient.

checks: Runtime fix: narration cut to 31 words (7 + 8 + 16) to fit about 15 seconds
Runtime fix: no event lands on the last word of any chapter, and there are fewer events overall
All facts come from the brief only. Nothing is invented about prices, times, rates or quotes
No digits are used. 'Two days' is written in words, as in the brief
None of the forbidden words (guarantee, always, never, best, lowest, save) are used
All six essential facts are in the brief, so there are no questions
No narration was supplied, so I drafted it in the owner's voice. It ends on the realistic outcome, offering the slot to another patient
process_flow fits because the weak link is reminder to parent, and the fix changes that link
All on-screen text is within its length limit
No em or en dashes are used
Each event's 'on' is 'start' or a single word copied exactly from that chapter's narration, in time order
